meta.document: Fairfield County, CT — no county government
meta.title: Fairfield County — the money trail
meta.note: Fairfield County has about 957,000 residents — the most populous county in Connecticut — but it has no county government at all. Connecticut abolished all eight of its county governments in 1960; the counties survive only as lines on a map for the courts. Everything a county elsewhere would do — schools, roads, police, social services — is run by the 23 towns and the state, and since 2022 the Census Bureau uses Connecticut’s regional Councils of Governments as the official county-equivalents. So there is no county budget to walk here: the money lives in the town budgets and the state budget. This page exists to say that plainly.
